skin_texture.roughness_basis: Reconstructed engineering value, not measured from a period person or calibrated capture.
skin_texture.identity_basis: Cleared reusable generic skin atlas; not a likeness, attested complexion, or source identifying any named/reconstructed resident.
skin_texture.uv_status: Source atlas and UV registration viewed in source diagnostics; final Blender export/LOD render validation remains outstanding.

hair_component.appearance_basis: Shared cleared CC0 short04 source fitted to existing Otis/Joseph/Martin bodies; hair/part/color are reconstructed choices, no period hairstyle attestation or individual likeness.

eye_components.source_basis: Actual helper centers/axes; original opaque sclera/iris/pupil, reconstructed dimensions and brown color, not resident facts

label: Reconstructed 1835 merchant's day dress (dark blue tailcoat, buff waistcoat, black stock, shirt collar points, pale trousers, black boots, black top hat) on the shared portable male rig
basis: Original shirt, waistcoat and tailcoat shells offset from the cleared adult body's own surface, tailcoat tails lofted round its sections, a stock lofted round its neck, trousers on the shared workwear shell, collar points laid on the jaw, a top hat seated round the skull and closed boots round the feet, cut after the day dress the reference pictures show (T-3449). Seams, ease, lengths and colours are reconstructed. Complete source anatomy remains unchanged beneath clothing.
source_scope: A British coat and trousers of about 1833 dressed with a waistcoat and stock in the Met (open access, in colour) give the cut of the tailcoat, waistcoat and trousers; Asher B. Durand's 1835 portrait of the New York merchant Luman Reed (Met) gives the stock, collar points and coat collar of a merchant in the scene year; Thomas Hornor's 1836 print of Broadway (Met) shows men in tailcoats and top hats at street distance. None is of Chicago or of Peck; no pixels or traced shapes enter the asset.

body_parameters.height_basis: The shared engineering body; the variation kit draws height and build at runtime. Not a recorded height.
body_parameters.age_basis: Engineering body at the kit base age 35, inside his recorded (reconstructed) age band 30-39; not aged further, since the town's merchants of 1835 were mostly young men and he is not placed in the town by this work.
body_parameters.shape_basis: CC0 male macro targets; equal software-category blend is engineering only, not inferred ancestry or a portrait.

proof_variants.body_basis: CC0 adult-male graphical body and the shared young light-skinned generic skin of the 1835 studies are reconstructed authoring choices. Philip F. W. Peck is an attested merchant; no picture of him has been read, and no complexion, height, face or outfit of his is asserted.

merchant_components.evidence_choice: The brief allowed a frock or a tail coat. The Met's coat of about 1833 is a cutaway tailcoat with a waistcoat showing at its opening; men on Broadway in 1836 wear tailcoats and top hats by day; Reed, a merchant painted in 1835, wears a high black stock with his collar points up. A tailcoat over a buff waistcoat, a stock and pale summer trousers joins the three for a merchant in July 1835.

provenance.source_scope: Reed (1835) shows a white shirt front in the waistcoat's opening; the 1833 ensemble a white front under its stock. Made only where it shows; the linen and its white are reconstructed.
Reed's portrait shows the shirt collar's two white points standing up at the cheeks above the stock; their size and angle are reconstructed.
A wide black stock wound high under the jaw, as Reed wears in 1835 and the 1833 ensemble is dressed with; its height and silk are reconstructed.

A single-breasted waistcoat with a rolled collar, cut straight at the waist and showing in the coat's opening and below its cutaway front, after the 1833 ensemble; the buff is that garment's, chosen for Peck, not recorded.

A double-breasted tailcoat cut square at the waist, broad lapels, a collar standing high behind the neck, tails to the back of the knee, after the 1833 coat; men on Broadway in 1836 wear the same. The dark blue (the 1833 coat's) and the gilt buttons are chosen; Peck's coat is not recorded.
Full pale trousers to the instep, as the 1833 linen trousers and the Broadway men's read; the stone colour is chosen for July (the 1833 straps under the foot are not modelled).
Black polished footwear under the trouser hem, as the 1833 ensemble shows; boots rather than shoes are a reconstructed choice (only the foot shows).
Men in tailcoats on Broadway (1836) wear black top hats with crowns flaring a little to the top and curled brims; the hat's height and brim are reconstructed.
